item.title: [155] /pcg/ - Pokémon Champions General
item.description:
MEGA SALAMENCE edtiton

Pokémon Champions is a free to play online battle simulator available on Switch and mobile. It features ranked, casual and private battles for both singles and doubles, and will be used for VGC tournaments in 2026.

>News
Pokemon Champions will undergo maintenance.
START: 9/9 @ 02:00 UTC
END: 9/9 @ 06:00 UTC

Reg MC is expected to be implemented during this time.

>Resources and useful links
Community Tournaments usage data: https://pikalytics.com/
Ladder usage data: https://pokechamdb.com/en

New Player Guide(NEW PEOPLE READ THIS):
https://rentry.org/pcg-guide (now taking suggestions and feedback)
Anon made guide for brand new players to make a viable team with the starting pokemon: https://teamsheet.gg/t/sample-beginner-reg-b-vl3698

Quick FAQ
>Do I need my own Pokémon to play?
No, the game features a recruitment system, but transferring from Home is recommended to save time and resources.
>What makes the game so much more accessible than before?
All aspects of a Pokémon are customizable with VP, a currency earned simply by playing the game. IVs are also removed.
Ask in the thread if you want any specific Pokémon, and someone will respond.
>Is there single player content?
No.
>Do I need a Nintendo Online subscription?
No.
>What's the starter pack?
US$6.99 one time purchase for 50 training tickets (fully train for free), 30 Teammate Tickets (recruit Pokemon without using VP), 50 extra box space and the LGPE trainer music. Only available on Switch for now.
>Is anything locked behind a paywall?
So far everything gameplay relevant is also purchasable with VP. Only E-Floette require ZA transfer.

item.title: [ 61] Finished my Marvel Silver Age read-through
item.description:
What's up /co/ random newfag here again! I did it! About one year and three months ago I decided to read comics from the start, beginning with Silver Age DC, which I wasnt a big fan of, and then moved on the the Marvel Silver Age, which took me about 11 months to read everything, + like 2 months to read the final spiderman issues because my delivery got fucked up and I had to wait for it an extra long time. First of all, its not even close, Marvel its just so much better in everything. I'm also reading the silver age runs for justice league/GL/Flash right now cause I got some free time and the difference is insane, even in the weaker marvel titles still clear most of the DC ones. I did not read EVERYTHING and skipped some characters according to the guide I'm using, and also read some others that I personally felt like it. These are my thoughts on what I read:
>Spider-Man
the best one and also not even close. even during the early days with Ditko I already was very impressed. I also gotta say the final issues (around 90 to 100) also had some amazing moments, and J. Jonah Jameson is now one of my favorite comic characters, everything he does and says was hilarious. I was also surprised by how MJ barely does anything and how Gwen is way more of a character than her early on, though I know that she will become more prominent in the title after Gwen bites the dust. I actually didnt care that much for Green Goblin and his issues, and think Doctor Octopus is way more of a threatening and cool villain, also surprised by Sandman being in like 2 or 3 issues and then becoming more of a FF villain instead. I did hear that after the Gerry Conway run the writing takes a nosedive for most of the 70s so if anyone wants to comment on it and if continuing to read everything after is worth it.
+

item.title: [ 58] MAGA TERRORISM: Attempted assassination of Ohio Gov. candidate Amy Acton foiled
item.description:
https://www.cleveland19.com/2026/09/06/multiple-people-injured-following-incident-involving-dr-amy-acton-canfield-fair/

CANFIELD, Ohio (WOIO) - An armed Canfield man was arrested Sunday at the Canfield Fair after lunging at Ohio gubernatorial candidate Dr. Amy Acton and injuring multiple people, according to campaign officials and sheriff’s deputies.

Records show Patrick Havas, 38, of Canfield, has been booked into the Mahoning County Jail on two counts of assault and one count of disorderly conduct.
What Happened

Gerry Ricciutti, a spokesperson for the Mahoning County Sheriff’s Office, said Havas walked around 2:30 p.m. into a tent for the Mahoning County Democrat Party (MCDP) and was taking cellphone video of Acton.

As Acton spoke to a crowd pf people, Ricciutti said Havas pushed his way through them, knocking two to the ground.

Havas was confronted by Acton’s security detail, which included Ohio State Highway Patrol troopers, and was arrested by Canfield police officers.

Ricciutti said deputies recovered two guns and a set of brass knuckles following his arrest. However, he said Havas did not use the weapons during the incident.

The highway patrol will be handling the investigation.

>Political Background and Reaction

>Voting records show Havas is a registered Republican. He has a criminal history including three theft charges and traffic offenses, according to court records.

“Let me be clear - The Mahoning County Democratic Party (MCDP) abhors political violence in all forms. What happened at our tent today during today’s visit from Dr. Acton is reprehensible and should be condemned by leaders on all sides of the aisle,” the MCDP chair said.

The Ohio gubernatorial race is one of the most high-profile races this year as the campaigns enter the final six weeks of campaigning before the general election in November.

item.title: [ 76] Fuel prices at record Labor Day high in US thanks to trump's failing Iran War
item.description:
https://apnews.com/article/labor-day-record-high-gas-prices-dffb7d3fa06ef930aaeebc380e5e4e0e

It’s never been more expensive in the U.S. to fill up the tank and take one last summer trip over the Labor Day weekend.

The average price of regular gas was $4.14 a gallon heading into the holiday, nearly a dollar higher than last year and well above the Labor Day weekend record of $3.82 from 2012, according to AAA motor club.

Nicole Collins planned to head from Philadelphia to South Carolina to visit friends, but she said her family has spent most of the summer close to home and not taking their typical weekend trips because driving has gotten so expensive.

“Gas is pretty high right now. It doesn’t help that we also have a baby, so we also have to pay for that,” Collins said outside a gas station in Claymont, Delaware, where regular gas was $4.199 a gallon.

Prices shot up after the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in February and have not settled down since. Crude oil traffic through the key Strait of Hormuz has plunged, and Iran has refused to reopen the waterway.

“Everything points to the Iran War and the Strait of Hormuz,” said Tom Seng, a professor of energy finance at Texas Christian University.

Energy Secretary Chris Wright offered few specifics on when the nation’s drivers might see relief at the gas pump, acknowledging that prices are higher now than Labor Day 2025.

But diesel is a different story: It hit a national average of $5.85 a gallon Friday, a record.

Trucks and other freight delivery systems use a lot of diesel, and that increased transportation cost is being passed on to consumers, whether at the grocery store or through package delivery services.

“It doesn’t really seem like there’s an end to it,” Collins said.

item.description:
Democrat Flock cameras could turn American neighborhoods into a ‘China-like surveillance state,’ ex-Pentagon AI chief warns
https://nypost.com/2026/09/05/tech/flock-cameras-could-create-china-like-surveillance-state-in-us/

Former Pentagon AI Policy Director Mark Beall warned that expanding artificial intelligence surveillance tools, like Flock cameras, could turn American communities into a “China-like surveillance state” unless guardrails are enforced.

Speaking on “Saturday in America,” Beall argued that while this technology can have vital law enforcement benefits, clear rules and judicial oversight are necessary to protect the rights of Americans at home.

“We have to be careful that we don’t go too far to the other direction and create a China-like surveillance state, which is literally what AI capabilities will ultimately enable and are enabling right now,” Beall told Fox News.

From destroyed camera poles to viral signs blocking surveillance lenses, some communities are pushing back against neighborhood surveillance cameras. Flock cameras are automated license plate readers used by law enforcement to record vehicle data that can aid criminal investigations. People in communities with the cameras have raised concerns about privacy and potential misuse by law enforcement.

Beall acknowledged that the technology can benefit law enforcement but said people’s privacy concerns are also valid. He urged a compromise and called for guardrails on how the cameras can be used, including strict rules and court oversight to prevent officers from abusing the technology for personal reasons.

“It’s tough to bring the message of compromise to the American people, especially when it comes to our constitutional protections,” Beall said.

item.title: [ 53] In Red States, Law-and-Order Republicans Turn Against Flock Cameras
item.description:
https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/05/us/red-states-republicans-flock-cameras.html

The Texas governor, Greg Abbott, directed police departments last week to stop spending state money on Flock Safety cameras, the license-plate readers that have drawn bipartisan backlash around the country.

Days later in Florida, Gov. Ron DeSantis’s administration ordered the systems removed from state roads. Mr. DeSantis has described the surveillance technology as “out of control.”

Both governors are tough-on-crime Republicans with deep backing from law enforcement agencies. Yet their moves underscore how the political winds are shifting against Flock and other plate-reading systems that have been embraced by police departments.

The cameras, which began rapidly appearing by the tens of thousands on American roads in recent years, track vehicles and feed surveillance databases. The networks of cameras can be used to assist officers by quickly locating vehicles connected with crimes. But concerns about a sweeping system of government surveillance and about abuses by individual officers have brought mounting opposition.

Flock cameras and others like them have become a campaign issue in several states, in some cases uniting Republicans and Democrats.

The result of the actions in Texas and Florida: Police departments are falling in line behind their governors and dismantling their license-plate readers. They have begun doing so even as they extol the cameras’ crime-fighting capabilities. In Jacksonville, Fla., the sheriff, a Republican, announced on Monday he was pausing his agency’s program of 150 cameras — one week after the office released a documentary-style video lauding their role in solving a kidnapping, among other crimes.

The moves in Texas and Florida are unfolding as Republican elected officials elsewhere are mulling their own restrictions.

item.title: [218] Lindsay Clancy Judge Says He’ll Declare a Mistrial
item.description:
Thread theme: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QkML_4j586Q

https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/lindsay-clancy-jury-hopelessly-deadlocked-mistrial-declared-rcna594052

A Massachusetts judge said he would declare a mistrial Friday after the jury weighing the fate of Lindsay Clancy failed for the third time to reach a verdict in the case of the mother accused of the strangling deaths of her three young children in 2023.

But in a dramatic courtroom moment, Clancy’s lawyer said he wanted to appeal to a higher court. The judge granted him one hour to do so.

Judge William Sullivan made the announcement after the jury sent the court a note saying it was still deadlocked.

“I’m going to declare a mistrial at this point,” Sullivan told the court Friday morning.

Both the prosecution and defense were given the opportunity to opine on the decision after the third deadlock.

Defense attorney Kevin Reddington fought hard against a mistrial, asking for a final emergency appeal to the Supreme Judicial Court of Massachusetts, but Sullivan seemed against bringing the jury back Saturday to continue deliberating should Reddington win the appeal.

Sullivan told Reddington he had one hour to file an emergency stay before calling the jurors back to dismiss them.

Clancy had pleaded not guilty to three first-degree murder charges in the deaths of Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months.

But the jury remained deadlocked after a nearly six-week trial and seven days of deliberation.

The jury was tasked with determining whether Clancy was criminally responsible in her children’s deaths, or whether she was not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility because of mental illness.

Sullivan got the first deadlock note Tuesday, the fourth day of deliberations, and dismissed the jurors after asking them to continue to work toward a verdict.

On Wednesday, the jury issued a second note saying it is “still unable to come to a unanimous decision.”

Quick Start Guide for First Timers:

Visa: Most countries get 90 days visa-free. Check if you need an eVisa or ARC if staying longer. Fill out your arrival card online before arriving for less stress.
Best Time: Oct–Dec for perfect weather (dry season). Avoid July–Sept typhoon season unless you like rain and chaos.
Getting Around: Taipei MRT is clean, cheap, and efficient as fuck. Youbike only needs an easy card and is essentially free unless you want to ride for hours.
High Speed Rail (HSR) for city hopping (Taipei Kaohsiung in ~1.5h).
Scooters are god outside Taipei. Get an international permit if you plan to ride.
Uber works but taxis are cheap. Avoid during rush hour or rain.

Food:

Night markets are mandatory. Shilin, Raohe, Ningxia, etc.
Must eats: Beef noodle soup, stinky tofu (acquired taste), oyster omelettes, bubble tea (original homeland), pineapple cake, mango shaved ice. All you can eat hotpot also.
7-11 and FamilyMart are better than in most countries, you can live off them if you want.

Top Spots:

Taipei: 101, Jiufen old street, Beitou hot springs, temples everywhere.
Taroko Gorge (east coast) — absolute kino nature.
Sun Moon Lake, Kenting (beaches), Alishan for mountains.
East coast for chill vibes and fewer tourists.

General Tips:

Taiwanese people are polite and helpful. Learn basic Mandarin or use Google Translate.
Tipping is not expected.
